title: The Hollow Choir
premise: Silas Voss has spent her life mapping the Thornfell mountains and the smuggler roads that thread them, keeping her head down and her heart locked away. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes in a single night, she learns the wards were never protecting the country from outside—they were holding a stolen kingdom inside, and the Hollow Choir, the voices of everyone erased to build it, are rising to reclaim their names. Guided by a disgraced ward-keeper named Ede and a runaway choir-child called Pip, Silas must chart a path through a land that is literally unmaking itself, choosing between restoring the false country she was born into and freeing the true one buried beneath. In the end she finds no door out—only a door through—and pays for it with her own name added to the Choir, though love, not duty, is what finally lets the others sing her back.
about_author: Coral Underhill is the pen name of a former trail guide who once got lost for three days in the Carpathians and came back with a notebook full of maps that made no sense. She writes fantasy about borders, both real and imagined, from a cabin she refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Silas Voss finishes a smuggling run through Thornfell and notices the stars have vanished mid-journey. At the waystation, she finds the border wards shattered and travelers unable to say where they've come from. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as her carefully invisible life begins to crack.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Silas's maps of Thornfell begin redrawing themselves overnight, towns sliding into places they never were. She seeks out Ede Marrow, a disgraced ward-keeper living in exile, who reveals the wards didn't keep enemies out—they imprisoned an erased nation beneath Thornfell. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your whole world is a forgery.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hums
chapters.summary: Fleeing a village that has forgotten its own name, Silas and Ede rescue Pip, a feral child who hums fragments of the Hollow Choir and can walk paths that no longer exist. Soldiers of the Provisional Council hunt anyone who remembers. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness—the first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: In Ede's hidden archive, the trio uncovers the founding lie: the kingdom of Vael was unmapped out of existence a century ago, its people folded into the Choir. The stars went out because the sky itself was part of the theft. POV: Ede. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve as Ede confronts his order's crime.

chapters.title: The Provisional Council
chapters.summary: Captured and brought before the Council, Silas is offered everything she ever pretended not to want—legitimacy, commission, safety—in exchange for mapping the last stable road so the regime can flee. She recognizes the trap: the road runs through the Choir's heart. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: duty seducing her precisely because it looks like belonging.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Silas betrays the Council's timetable and leads Pip and Ede along smuggler roads that respond to memory, each mile costing a recollection. Pip's humming steadies them; Silas loses her memory of her mother's face. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief as payment, and the growing certainty that some things are worth forgetting.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir Rises
chapters.summary: At the sunken capital of Vael, the Choir manifests—thousands of faceless voices demanding their names back—and the land above begins folding into it. Ede tries to bargain with the voices using forbidden ward-craft and is nearly unmade. POV: Ede. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into awe at the scale of what was stolen.

chapters.title: The Door Through
chapters.summary: Pip reveals she is the Choir's first stolen child, its living key: there is no door out of the dying country, only a door through to restore Vael. Opening it requires a name freely given to anchor the new beginning. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: a child's clarity cutting through adult fear.

chapters.title: Silas Voss, Freely Given
chapters.summary: As the Council's soldiers and the collapsing land converge, Silas gives her name to the door, dissolving into the Choir while Ede holds the threshold and Pip sings her through. The false Thornfell peels away like old paint. POV: alternating Silas and Ede. Emotional beat: climax—love against duty, sacrifice against erasure.

chapters.title: Every Name Sung Back
chapters.summary: Vael stands restored under returned stars; the Choir members wake with their names, and Pip—now a girl with a history—chooses to stay with Ede. A voice in the dawn chorus sings a melody only Silas would know, and someone with ink-stained fingers knocks at Ede's door. POV: Ede. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging earned, family found, love sung home.
